title: Tadej Pogacar welcomes Remco Evenepoel’s Tour of Flanders debut
content:
Tadej Pogacar has welcomed Remco Evenepoel’s debut participation in Sunday’s Tour of Flanders and revealed he told Jonas Vingegaard that he should race the spring Classics too.

Evenepoel’s surprise announcement on Wednesday, of his plan to ride his country’s most famous race for the first time, added another wrinkle to the expected three-way fight between Pogacar, Mathieu van der Poel, and Wout Van Aert.

A two-time winner of Liege-Bastogne-Liege, and seemingly blessed with a profile well-suited to the Ronde’s sharp climbs and cobbles, Evenepoel’s appearance has been covered with mania in cycling-mad Flanders.

The Tour of Flanders is a one-day cobbled Classic set to take part over 278.2 kilometers in the west of Belgium, with the women’s race covering 164.1km in the same area.

“I think from my side, it’s good to have a rider like Remco, always wanting to go from far out, racing hard far from the finish and always on the attack,” Pogacar said in his press conference from the team hotel on Friday.

“We saw from the last few races that he’ll go for the win no matter what. I think he can do a really great race on Sunday, I think he’s in good shape. I’ll have to watch out for his long-range attacks — and just not let him out of my sight.”

Like Pogacar, Evenepoel has gained a reputation for his willingness to attack early as part of cycling’s ultra-aggressive new generation. Unlike Pogacar, however, who is able to create separation with his supreme acceleration on the climbs, Evenepoel’s biggest advantage is his power output on the flat.

The world’s best time triallist, due in large part to his incredible aerodynamicism, even if Pogacar drops him on the climbs, Evenepoel at his best has the ability to bridge back on the flat. Equally, should he get his own gap — he is particularly aggressive in crosswinds — the Belgian is extremely difficult to chase down.

“(Evenepoel) can attack in most random place and you need to be ready for that,” said Pogacar.  “You can never let him go in the front with a couple of seconds because it’s almost impossible to catch him back because he’s so fast. Remco can attack on the flattest section of the race and then he can make a gap.”

Evenepoel’s participation means four of cycling’s so-called big five will be on the startline on Sunday — the only man missing is Pogacar’s Grand Tour rival Jonas Vingegaard.

Having put on muscle and demonstrated improved acceleration last season, Vingegaard looks as if he could produce excellent results in the spring classics — but has historically always avoided them in favour of shorter one-week stage races. This year, he won Paris-Nice and the Volta a Catalunya in preparation for next month’s Giro d’Italia, the only Grand Tour he is yet to win.

“I told Jonas in 2023 when we finished stage 20 (of the Tour) at the Markstein that the way he’s riding, all three weeks, why doesn’t he come to try to race the Classics?” Pogacar added.

“With the kind of shape he is in at the Tour, I think he can race for the victory in the biggest Classics of the year.”

Pogacar, who has won the past two editions of the Tour of Flanders, is bidding to become the first rider to sweep the Monuments this season, having finally won Milan-Sanremo on his sixth attempt after four previous top five finishes.

The only Monument he has never won is Paris-Roubaix, which will take place in northern France next Sunday.
